resources.string: Displays Alpha Ophiuchi as “Hou” in Chinese and uses the standard Chinese name for Gouxian Yi. Adds Iota Aurigae and Gamma Pegasi. The star visibility list is sorted from brighter to dimmer magnitudes. A slider below the sky chart zooms out on the left and in on the right. Pinch zoom is disabled. Drag with one finger to pan, while star points and the pointing marker keep their screen size. Tapping nearby objects opens a choice list. A solid red triangle marks an aligned direction outside the view. When existing label placement cannot fit every name, the minimum zoom prioritizes stars of magnitude 1.0 or brighter, the Sun and Moon, then reveals dimmer names as the chart zooms in. Selected-object details show rise and set times, or indicate when an object stays above the horizon all day or does not rise that day. Stars are identified as circumpolar or never-rising when applicable. Reverses the route zoom slider direction in Status. Desktop buttons share consistent size, spacing and corner radius across apps, reserve enough top inset for the complete outline, and grow with system text size. Music, Device communication and Color vision simulator use the toolbox background, transparent system bars, and the same title and subtitle format as other apps. Earthquake details use concise geographic labels without appending provider wording.
